components.name: Logo
components.description: Ascendum logo. Size matches Logo.jsx (full = wordmark lockup, compact = mark only). Colours are deliberately NOT bound to mode variables — a logo should be chosen explicitly, not recoloured by a mode switch. WARNING: the Inverted mark has no backing layer; its glyph is transparent and reads only against a dark surface. On anything light the glyph disappears. Assets were scaled to a common height so toggling Inverted does not resize the component.

components.name: Avatar
components.description: Initials avatar. Department gradients are paint styles, so they do NOT respond to Light/Dark — which is why the initials bind to text/on-gradient-*, fixed in both modes. Digital is the one light gradient and takes dark text. For photo avatars, place an image fill on the instance; the circular clip is already set.

components.name: Badge
components.description: Status pill. Uses feedback/*-bg for tints; the source used the slightly stronger *-border values for four of them, a difference of a few percent that was not worth eight extra tokens. The dot inherits the label colour.

components.name: Button
components.description:
Ascendum button. Sharp 0px corners against 20px cards is the brand signature — never round these. Outline fills solid on hover. Padding, radius, stroke weight and type size are all mode-responsive: switch the Dimension mode rather than overriding values.

ICON SLOT — 'Leading icon' toggles visibility, 'Icon' swaps the glyph. Deliberately not a variant axis; making it one would take 24 variants to 48.

COLOUR CAVEAT — a swapped icon inherits its colour from the icon component, not from this button's label token. That is correct for Outline and Ghost in Default, Focus and Disabled. It is WRONG for Solid, and for Hover on any style, where the label inverts to milkyway but the icon would stay midnight. In those cases apply a colour override to the icon on the canvas. Figma exposes no way to pre-bind this per variant once the node is driven by an instance-swap property.

components.name: Checkbox
components.description: 20px box, 1.5px border, 3px corner — tighter than the 4px field radius. Checked and indeterminate both fill with border/strong so the mark inverts correctly in dark mode.

components.name: Divider
components.description: 1px rule bound to border/default. Not in the source CSS as a named class — dividers were inline borders. Formalised here so the hairline colour has one owner.

components.name: Input
components.description: Form field. 1.5px border and 4px radius — the quiet middle ground between the sharp button and the round card. ERROR COLOUR — resolved decision: status errors use feedback/error (#b02a32), the value DESIGN.md declares. The source CSS used the Products department red (#de4b54) here; that is being corrected in the stylesheet, not mirrored in Figma.

components.name: Radio
components.description: 20px ring, 1.5px border, 9px selected dot. Same geometry as Checkbox but fully round.

components.name: Skeleton
components.description: Loading placeholder. Solid fill bound to bg/skeleton so it works in both modes. The source's animated shimmer gradient is code-side only — Figma cannot animate, and a gradient paint style would be stuck in light mode.

components.name: Slider
components.description: 3px track, 18px thumb with a 3px inner ring. SIMPLIFIED: the source adds an outer 1.5px midnight ring via box-shadow; Figma cannot bind an effect colour to a variable, so that ring is omitted rather than hardcoded. Fill width and thumb position are instance-level overrides.

components.name: SectionTag
components.description: Department tag. Square corners, asymmetric padding (10px left, 12px right) so the swatch sits tighter to the edge. The swatch is the only place department colour appears as a flat fill — everywhere else it belongs in a gradient. Text must be typed in caps; Figma has no text-transform.

components.name: Toggle
components.description: 44x24 track, 17px knob inset 2px. Knob position is driven by auto-layout alignment rather than an absolute offset, so it stays correct if the track is ever resized. On-state knob uses text/inverted so it flips with the mode. Knob inset is 3.5px horizontally — the 1.5px border plus the source's 2px offset, since CSS measures that offset from the padding edge.

components.name: Alert
components.description: Inline feedback banner. NOTE: the source styled the warning tone with a purple tint (#faf3fd / #ead8f3) — the Mortgages department colour — rather than amber. That contradicts DESIGN.md, so this uses feedback/warning-bg. Padding rounded from 18/22 to 20/24 for the 4px grid.

components.name: Breadcrumb Item
components.description: One step in a breadcrumb trail, with its trailing separator. Set Separator=False on the last item. Current is Bold; links are muted until hover. Separator uses icon/muted — the source's #c0c0c0 had no semantic equivalent.

components.name: Code Block
components.description: THIN REPRESENTATION — syntax highlighting and line numbers live in code. NOTE: the source sets code in Barlow (var(--font-sans)), not a monospace face, which is consistent with DESIGN.md's rule that Barlow is the only typeface. components.name: Jira Annotation
components.description:
Jira-powered annotation panel for design review.
Brings Jira context directly into Figma while preserving Ascendum Design System styling and structure. Populate using the shared Jira Annotation Agent skill and Atlassian connector. Jira remains the source of truth; Objective, Review Focus, Design Requirements, and Acceptance Criteria are semantically derived from the Jira work item.


//INSTRUCTIONS


First-time setup only
Open Figma Agent.
Click Add context → Connectors → Atlassian.
Connect your Atlassian account.
When Atlassian asks which site to authorize, select the site that contains the Jira project you are working on.
For each Jira ticket
Insert Jira Annotation from the Ascendum Design System.
Select the annotation component on the canvas.
Open Figma Agent.
Run the /populate-jira-annotation skill.
In the same message, provide the actual Jira issue key for the ticket you want to display.

For example, if your real Jira ticket is RAIL-248, type:
/populate-jira-annotation @Atlassian RAIL-248
You can also paste the full URL of the actual Jira ticket instead of the issue key.
Important: Do not type ABC-123, JIRA-123, PROJ-1234, <JIRA-KEY>, or any other example shown in documentation. These are placeholders, not real Jira tickets. Always replace them with the key or URL of the Jira ticket you are currently working on.
The Agent will retrieve the Jira ticket, populate the annotation, adjust the number of requirement and acceptance-criteria rows, apply the appropriate priority treatment, and link the Open Jira button to that ticket.
Do not detach the annotation component.
